promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: INPUT 1: the sheet of four faces to paint (layout authority)
Image 2: INPUT 2: the same ship already painted: the finish to match (material only)

Use case: precise-object-edit / texture reskin of a technical render sheet.
INPUT 1 is a sheet of FOUR separate orthographic renders of parts of one gun arm of a 3D spacecraft (a Hegemony XIV Onslaught-class battleship, a heavily armoured low-tech capital ship, properly maintained picket flagship on station), the first seen from directly above with the bow at the top of the tile and the other three seen square-on from the port side with the bow to the left, each drawn alone as flat-coloured shapes on a plain flat mid-blue background:
top-left: the arm's nose deck: a round brown-grey turret housing low in the tile, a dark brown stepped plate at the top with a small square hatch, mid-tan bone-brown plates on the right, a dark grey strip and small orange slivers at the right edge;
top-right: the forward flank: a warm brown-grey upper band with dark brown and bone-brown plates, then a bright orange rail with dark grey straps and weathered burnt-orange plates at both ends;
bottom-left: the lower flank: weathered burnt-orange and bright orange plates at left with a dark grey strap and a mid-tan bone-brown strip below, then dark charcoal grey sponson armour with a large cool blue-grey steel plate and a near-black recess at right;
bottom-right: the arm's nose side: a warm brown-grey face with a dark brown wedge plate and bone-brown plates, a large dark charcoal grey cheek plate below and to the left, a dark grey vertical strap, and weathered burnt-orange plates at the bottom right.
INPUT 2 is the SAME ship, already painted: it is the finish to match. Use its paint colours, its maintained service finish, its seam and fastener treatment. Never copy INPUT 2's composition, view or shapes.

Paint every shape in INPUT 1 as that maintained armoured surface. This image will be cut into its four tiles and projected back onto the 3D model as a texture, so geometry must not move:
- Keep the four tiles exactly where they are, the same size, with the same plain blue gutters between them. Do not zoom, crop, shift, rotate, enlarge or shrink anything. Every shape occupies exactly the same pixels as in INPUT 1, with exactly the same outline, and any hole, gap or slot stays plain background blue. Thin isolated slivers and strips stay where they are.
- Every shape is a flat painted steel armour plate. Add painted surface detail inside each plate's outline only: crisp plate seams and welded joints, neat rows of small fasteners and rivets, flush access panels, a light even film of dust and grime in the seams and a few small scuffs on plate edges. Nothing may stand out from the surface or cross an outline.
- Keep EVERY plate in its own colour as INPUT 1 assigns it. The alternating plate tones are deliberate and must stay distinct, never evened out or blended: warm brown-grey plates stay warm brown-grey; dark brown plates stay dark chocolate brown; bone-brown plates stay a MEDIUM dusty greyish tan: clearly darker than bone white, never cream, off-white or pale, about halfway between the warm brown-grey plates and bone white (INPUT 1 draws them lighter than the paint really is: the pale tan plates in INPUT 1 are this medium tan); bright orange plates stay saturated Hegemony orange enamel; the duller darker orange plates stay a weathered burnt orange; dark grey armour (straps, frames, coamings, sponson plates) stays dark charcoal grey; blue-grey steel plates stay a cool blue-grey steel; near-black recesses and seams stay near-black. Do not repaint any plate another colour, add no stripes and no differently coloured patches.
- Exposure: match INPUT 2's paint values, not INPUT 1's. INPUT 1 is rendered brighter than the paint; every plate on this sheet is painted about one step darker than it is drawn in INPUT 1. In particular the bone-brown plates are a MEDIUM dusty tan like corrugated cardboard, the same value as the tan plates on INPUT 2's arm decks: never cream, beige-white, off-white or pale.
- The ship is maintained, not battered. Weathering is light and even across every plate. No rust, no repair patches, no soot, scorch marks, burns, streaks, impact damage, dents, holes, large stains, chipped bare metal, or any single concentrated area of wear. No lettering, numbers, markings, decals, logos or hazard stripes.
- Lighting: flat, even, shadowless, like an albedo/diffuse texture map. No cast shadows, no ambient-occlusion darkening, no specular highlights, no reflections, no rim light, no bright bevelled edge highlights, no directional light, no gradients across a plate.
- Background and gutters: the same plain flat uniform mid-blue as INPUT 1, with no floor, shadow, vignette, text, labels or borders.
Output: one landscape 16:9 image, same composition as INPUT 1.

agentMessages: I’ll use the imagegen skill to reskin the four-face sheet, keeping its layout and plate colours intact while matching the ship’s finish.
